original_question: Determine whether the gamma_3-flow is nontrivial, that is, whether the induced change of a Poisson bivector is more than a coordinate change along a vector field X_{gamma_3}^d on R^d.
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting the introductory open problem in Section 1: for Kontsevich’s tetrahedral cocycle gamma_3 acting on the Nambu–Poisson class, is the induced deformation genuinely nontrivial, or does it come only from an infinitesimal coordinate change along a vector field X_{gamma_3}^d on R^d? The paper later writes the trivial case explicitly as the coboundary identity Q_{gamma_3}^d(P⊗4) = [[P, X_{gamma_3}^d(P⊗3)]]. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the central issue as the (non)triviality of the gamma_3-flow, correctly interprets triviality as ‘just a coordinate change,’ and correctly names the trivializing vector field X_{gamma_3}^d on R^d. Those are exactly the deformation-theoretic ingredients singled out in the introduction. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))
missing_details: The paper is not about arbitrary Poisson bivectors: it restricts to the Nambu–Poisson brackets of determinant type (1) on affine real space R^d. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))

The bracket must be specified as {f,g}_d(x) = rho(x) det(∂(f,g,a_1,...,a_{d-2})/∂(x_1,...,x_d)), with x = (x_1,...,x_d) and Casimirs a_i in C^1(R^d). Your draft omits rho, the Casimirs, and the determinant/Jacobian form. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))

The deformation in question is specifically Kontsevich’s tetrahedral graph-cocycle flow, written in the paper as Pdot = Q_{gamma_3}(P⊗4), not an unspecified flow attached to gamma_3. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))

The paper’s exact algebraic test for triviality is the Schouten-bracket coboundary equation Q_{gamma_3} = [[P, X_{gamma_3}]]; the coordinate-change wording in your draft is correct but not fully stand-alone without this formula or the identification of [[.,.]] as the Schouten bracket. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))

The paper’s higher-dimensional scope is the Nambu–Poisson setting on R^{d>3}; it also records that trivializing fields are already known for d = 2, 3, and 4, so the live research issue is the higher-dimensional regime. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))

The vector field X_{gamma_3}^d is sought as a differential-polynomial object encoded by Nambu micro-graphs, written in the paper as X_{gamma_3}^{d>2}(rho,a); your draft does not say that the sought trivialization is within this differential-polynomial/micro-graph framework. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))

No homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, positive-characteristic, or formal-power-series assumptions belong to this paper’s formulation of the problem. To be stand-alone and paper-faithful, the question should explicitly stay in the affine real Nambu–Poisson/Jacobian-determinant setting and not leave the ambient category implicit. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))
refined_question: Let d > 3 be fixed, and let P be a Nambu–Poisson bivector on affine R^d determined by the Jacobian-determinant bracket {f,g}_d(x) = rho(x) det(∂(f,g,a_1,...,a_{d-2})/∂(x_1,...,x_d)), where a_1,...,a_{d-2} are Casimirs. For Kontsevich’s tetrahedral graph cocycle gamma_3, does the induced tetrahedral flow Pdot = Q_{gamma_3}^d(P⊗4) define a genuinely nontrivial infinitesimal deformation of P on this Nambu–Poisson class, or does there exist a differential-polynomial vector field X_{gamma_3}^d(P⊗3) on R^d such that Q_{gamma_3}^d(P⊗4) = [[P, X_{gamma_3}^d(P⊗3)]], where [[.,.]] is the Schouten bracket, so that the deformation is only an infinitesimal coordinate change? ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for a Nambu–Poisson bracket P of the determinant form (1) on affine R^d, decide whether the tetrahedral gamma_3-flow is a Poisson coboundary, i.e. whether one can solve Q_{gamma_3}^d(P⊗4) = [[P, X_{gamma_3}^d(P⊗3)]]. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))
justification: The draft does not match Proposition 1 itself; rather, it matches the open deformation-theoretic question stated in the introduction. Section 1 first fixes the Nambu–Poisson bracket (1), then asks whether the gamma_3-flow is nontrivial, understood as being more than a coordinate change along X_{gamma_3}^d. Section 2 makes the equivalent coboundary criterion explicit via Q_{gamma_3} = [[P, X_{gamma_3}]]. Proposition 1 is nearby context because it constrains the vanishing micro-graphs used in the search for such X in higher dimensions, and the page-95 bullet list shows that the paper’s later open questions are structural questions about how X_{gamma_3}^{d+1} might be built if the flow is trivial. So the sharpest paper-faithful rewrite keeps the nontriviality/coboundary question, but narrows it to the determinant-type Nambu–Poisson class on affine R^d and writes the actual operator equation explicitly. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))
